item.title: Свобода — еще не возможность
item.description: Грамотность — краеугольный камень любого общества, в котором существует свобода слова. Свидетельством тому — не только статистика, но и сами жизни тех, кому труднее всего. Рассказывает Доминик Бербидж.

item.title: How Pakistan’s blasphemy laws trigger violence
item.description: Since the passage of Pakistan's blasphemy law in 1987, there have been dozens of extra judicial murders of individuals accused of blasphemy. Perpetrators of this vigilante justice rarely face consequences. Helen Haft and Joelle Fiss examine the repercussions of this law and its impact on free speech.

item.title: Self-inculpatory laws do not exist
item.description: Antoon De Baets argues that criminal states do not punish themselves.

item.title: Self-inculpatory laws exist
item.description: Eric Heinze argues that states can and do proclaim their own past and present wrongdoings, even when international law does not strictly require it.

item.title: Criminal regimes are never soft on history
item.description: Antoon De Baets argues that states that sacrifice their citizens first, sacrifice their history next.

item.title: Social media for revolution?
item.description: New forms of popular protest require a new digital response.
